text: The Hessenlied is the official anthem of the German state of Hesse. The lyrics were authored by Carl Preser (1828–1910), and the melody was composed by Albrecht Brede (1834–1920). The song begins with the lines "I know a land so affluent and so beautiful, the fields full of golden grain," describing a landscape where forests "flourish from the valley to sunny heights" and "many dark, fragrant forests" are present. It recalls the speaker's childhood memories of sitting "in blossoms and flowers" under the care of their mother's hand. The anthem then expresses a greeting to the homeland as "thou magnificent land," calling Hesse "the heart of Germany, my thriving land Hesse." The geographical scope is defined as stretching "from the Main to the Weser, Werra and Lahn," with the text noting that the cities in this region "shine" and are "gorgeous to see in the light." The repeated lines emphasize both personal nostalgia and regional pride. This article about the music of Germany is a stub. You can help Wikipedia by adding missing information.
